newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks in London firm, Dow seen higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks in London firm, Dow seen higher.

text.p: U.S. stocks in London were mostly firmer in modest trading on Monday, lifted by Wall Street's higher close on Friday and firm U.S. Treasuries.

Dealers said they expected the Dow Jones Industrial Average, which closed 0.24 percent higher at 6007.02 on Friday, to start the week some 10 to 12 points higher although potential would likely be blocked by caution ahead of a slew of data.

"Most prices (in London) are looking $1/8 or $1/4 higher and press comment over the weekend was mostly favourable, except for Garzarelli. But we think she's right about there being little movement before the election," one dealer said.
Elaine Garzarelli, best known for predicting the October 1987 Wall Street crash, repeated her prediction that the U.S. market could drop by between 15 percent and 25 percent by the end of this year.
In an interview with Germany's Der Spiegel magazine, she forecast a drop after the November 5 U.S. presidential election.

Dealers said her comments were having little immediate impact. This week's data, which includes third-quarter employment cost index, October consumer confidence, third-quarter preliminary gross domestic product and Friday's key October jobs report, was drawing investors' attention.
Among major movers, American Express was up $1/4 at $47. Other gainers included Intel, up $3/8 at $105-3/4 and Gillette, which gained $1/4 to $73-3/4.
McDonald's was up $1/4 at $44-7/8 on recent bullish comments from analysts on its growth prospects, dealers said.
"There was a report in Barron's, which initially looked positive, but just highlighted the intense competition and overcapacity in the beer market," one trader said.
